question: Why did the static magnetic field promote single-crystal formation of sodium chlorate at high humidity?
expect: premise false: no measurable field effect; single crystals become more frequent at RH 59% independent of the applied field (abstract; Discussion)
rendered:
Document: [Evaporative Crystallization of Sodium Chlorate Droplets under Controlled Humidity in the Presence of a Static Magnetic Field]

The static magnetic field did not promote single-crystal formation of sodium chlorate at high humidity. The results showed that the deposition morphology strongly depends on relative humidity, with irregular patterns at low humidity, coffee-ring structures at intermediate humidity, and single-crystal formation at high humidity. The applied magnetic field did not have a measurable effect on the deposition process under the investigated conditions.

The correct answer is that the static magnetic field did not promote single-crystal formation of sodium chlorate at high humidity.
